# AlphaMine

Native client of **Minecraft Alpha 1.0.16** written as a VoxelCore 0.31 content pack, talking to the
original Java server (Alpha SMP 0.1.1, protocol 14), with a frame-to-frame (F2F) harness that compares
screenshots of the Java client and the VoxelCore port pixel by pixel. The plan and status live in the
VoxelCore directory: `D:\Prog\VoxelCore\voxelcore-0.31.0_pre_gemini\agents\ALPHAMINE.md` and `agents\F2F.md`.

## Layout

| Path | What | Tracked |
|---|---|---|
| `ref/` | RetroMCP 1.2 workspace: client `minecraft/src`, server `minecraft_server/src`, clean decompilation `*/src_original`, `conf/` (mappings), `options.cfg` | sources and config only |
| `tables/` | block/item tables generated from the Java sources (`gen_tables.py`), `NOTES.md` explains fields | yes |
| `golden/` | reference snapshots/dumps of the Java client per scenario (F2F); worlds `world_a`, `world_b`, `devworld` (developer world: every Alpha block in rows, generated by `tools/alphamine/gen_devworld.py`, layout in `devworld/devworld_layout.json`, see `agents/ALPHAMINE.md` §10) | yes |
| `engine/` | VoxelCore F2F patch and build script; binaries ignored | patches/scripts |
| `assets/` | textures/sounds extracted from the jar and the asset index (`extract_assets.py`) | no, regenerated |
| `logs/`, `shots/`, `runs/` | run logs, screenshots | no |

Changes to the Java client/server go only through `ref/` sources and patches against `src_original`.

## Restoring the RetroMCP workspace

A clone has only sources. The full working copy (jars, libraries, builds, worlds) is backed up at
`D:\Backups\alphamine_dec` (**read-only, never modify**).

1. Copy the ignored parts from the backup into `ref\` (PowerShell):
   ```
   $b = 'D:\Backups\alphamine_dec'; $r = 'D:\Prog\AlphaMine\ref'
   robocopy "$b\jars" "$r\jars" /E
   robocopy "$b\libraries" "$r\libraries" /E
   copy "$b\RetroMCP-Java-CLI.jar" $r
   robocopy "$b\minecraft\game" "$r\minecraft\game" /E /XC /XN /XO
   robocopy "$b\minecraft_server\game" "$r\minecraft_server\game" /E /XC /XN /XO
   ```
   Without the backup: download RetroMCP-Java 1.2 CLI, run `java -jar RetroMCP-Java-CLI.jar setup`
   (choose `a1.0.16`; it downloads the client/server jars, libraries and the asset index into `jars\`
   and `libraries\`), then restore `minecraft\src` and `minecraft_server\src` from git (setup + decompile
   would overwrite them with the clean decompilation).
2. Check `ref\options.cfg`: `workingDir=D:\Prog\AlphaMine\ref`.
3. Build and run with JDK 8 (`C:\Program Files\Java\jdk1.8.0_481`), from PowerShell:
   ```
   cd D:\Prog\AlphaMine\ref
   java -jar RetroMCP-Java-CLI.jar recompile      # client + server, ~1 min, "Finished successfully"
   java -jar RetroMCP-Java-CLI.jar start server   # port 25565, offline mode
   java -jar RetroMCP-Java-CLI.jar start client   # 854x480, connects to localhost:25565 (patched GuiMainMenu)
   ```
   Stop the Java processes after a run: only your own (`am_server stop`, `am_client stop` in the harness stop the
   server tagged `-Dalphamine.dir=<dir>` and the client on that F2F port). `Get-Process java | Stop-Process` also kills
   servers of other agents/ports.
   While a server from `minecraft_server\bin` is running, rebuild only the client:
   `powershell -File ref\compile_client.ps1 F2FAgent.java EntityRenderer.java ...` (javac into `minecraft\bin`;
   RetroMCP `recompile` rebuilds both sides and ignores `--side`).

## Assets and tables

The scripts live in the VoxelCore directory (`tools\alphamine\`, Python 3 stdlib only) and run from WSL:

```
VC=/mnt/d/Prog/VoxelCore/voxelcore-0.31.0_pre_gemini
python3 $VC/tools/alphamine/gen_tables.py       # ref/minecraft/src -> tables/{blocks,items,textures_by_block}.json, NOTES.md
python3 $VC/tools/alphamine/extract_assets.py   # jar + asset index -> assets/ (+ named tiles from tables/)
```

`extract_assets.py` writes every resource of `minecraft.jar` under its original path, sounds under
`assets/sound/<index name>` (resolved by hash from `jars/assets/objects`), 16x16 tiles of `terrain.png`
and `gui/items.png` as `assets/tiles/{terrain,items}/<row*16+col>.png`, tiles named by the block table as
`assets/named/{blocks,items}/<name>.png`, and `assets/manifest.json` (path, size, sha1, source).
`gen_tables.py` executes the Java registrations with a small interpreter (`minijava.py`) instead of
pattern matching; anything it cannot evaluate is listed in `tables/NOTES.md`.

## F2F client

The Java client has a frame-to-frame test mode (spec: `agents\F2F.md` in the VoxelCore directory). Without
the flag nothing changes: every hook falls through to the original code (checked: auto-connect, window,
options.txt as before).

**Start** (from WSL or PowerShell; both scripts start Java detached through WMI and print the java PID;
logs go to `logs\<LogName>.log/.err`, cp866):
```
powershell -File D:\Prog\AlphaMine\ref\start_server.ps1 -Dir D:\Prog\AlphaMine\run\server   # nogui; dir holds server.properties, ops.txt, world\
powershell -File D:\Prog\AlphaMine\ref\start_client.ps1 -F2F 25570 [-Size 854x480] [-Server localhost:25565] [-AssetIndex a1.0.14-local]
```
`-AssetIndex a1.0.14-local` (the harness default, created by `am_client`): a copy of the asset index whose 13 `custom`
entries point to local `file:` copies of what their https URLs return (a 536-byte "301 Moved" page), so launchwrapper
no longer re-downloads them on every start: ~2 s to F2F `hello` instead of 22-40 s, same files for the game.
`start_client.ps1` builds the same classpath as `RetroMCP start client` (libraries + `minecraft\bin` +
`deobfuscated.jar`, `-Djava.library.path=libraries\natives`, cwd `minecraft\game`) but uses the main class
`net.minecraft.src.F2FLaunch`, which turns `--f2f PORT`, `--f2f-size WxH` and `--server HOST:PORT` into the
system properties `f2f.port`, `f2f.size`, `f2f.server` and passes the rest to launchwrapper (launchwrapper has
its own `--server`, so ours must not reach it). Without `-F2F` the main menu auto-connects to `-Server` as
before; **in F2F mode it does not auto-connect** — the harness sends `connect` (default host/port from `--server`).
Do not use `Start-Process -RedirectStandardOutput` from WSL: java inherits the interop pipe and the caller hangs.

**What F2F mode does** (classes `F2F*` in `minecraft/src/net/minecraft/src`):
- `F2FAgent`: TCP `127.0.0.1:PORT`, one JSON line per request/response; commands run on the main thread,
  `Minecraft.run` calls `F2FAgent.serve()` instead of its frame. Commands: `hello`, `mode`, `step`, `input`,
  `state`, `shot`, `chat`, `gui`, `wait`, `connect`, `quit`. Between commands the last frame is re-shown and a
  KeepAlive is sent once a second, so an idle client is not dropped by the server.
- `F2FFrame`: the game renders into an FBO of fixed size (color texture + 24-bit depth); `shot` reads that FBO
  (`glReadPixels`) into a PNG and returns sha256 of the RGB bytes; the window gets a copy for viewing only.
  `displayWidth/Height` are pinned to the FBO size.
- `F2FKeyboard`/`F2FMouse`: facades for every LWJGL input read (`Minecraft.runTick`, `GuiScreen`, `MouseHelper`,
  `EntityRenderer`); in F2F mode input comes only from `input`/`gui`, the cursor is never grabbed, focus loss
  never pauses (`EntityRenderer`, `setIngameFocus`).
- `F2FClock`: virtual time, 50 ms per tick, advanced only by `step`/`wait`/`gui` (replaces the clocks in
  `runTick`, `EntityRenderer`, `RenderGlobal` block-break pulse, `GuiMainMenu` splash, `LoadingScreenRenderer`).
- `F2FRandom`: all client `new Random()` (Entity, EffectRenderer, GuiIngame, EntityRenderer, World, RenderItem,
  RenderPainting, NetClientHandler, Item, BlockChest, GuiMainMenu) and all 48 `Math.random()` calls (TextureFX,
  particles, entities, blocks) are seeded; `mode {seed}` reseeds them.
- `mode` also resets tick-dependent visual state: tick/frame counters, `ticksRan`, `GuiIngame` counters (and
  chat with `clear_chat`; `prevVignetteBrightness` set to its fixed point `clamp(1 - brightness)` since 01.10, E2E),
  cloud counter, chunk sort position, `rendererUpdateCount`, TextureFX arrays (water,
  lava, fire), particles, player bobbing, entity RNGs by entity id. So a shot depends only on world, position,
  seed and the ticks/input after `mode`, not on how long connecting/loading took.
- Occlusion queries are off; `updateRenderers` rebuilds every dirty chunk in the frustum each frame; options
  are not loaded from/saved to `options.txt` (defaults; override with `mode {options:{renderDistance:1,...}}`);
  skins are not downloaded (default `char.png`); memory numbers in the menu/F3 are fixed; `debug` fps line fixed.
- `wait` paces ticks to the wall clock (50 ms) by default, because the server and the network run in real time.
- `render {all, layers:{sky, clouds, terrain, water, entities, particles, weather, selection, hand, hud, gui, fog,
  lighting}, clear:[r,g,b]}` (`F2FRender`): render only chosen layers; a layer that is off draws neither colour nor
  depth; `clear` is used while `sky` is off; `lighting:false` forces vertex colour 1.0 while chunks compile. Default:
  everything on (without `--f2f` every gate is open). Details: `agents\F2F.md` §7.1.

**Patches** (in `ref\patches\`): `f2f-client.patch` — whole client diff against `minecraft/src_original`
(includes the older non-F2F edits: fire in `BlockFire`/`RenderBlocks`, main-menu auto-connect and the
"bebra228" button); `f2f-only.patch` — only the F2F changes on top of those. Both checked with `patch -p1`
(result identical to `minecraft/src`). The server has its own F2F test mode: see "F2F lockstep server" below.

**Harness** (VoxelCore directory): `tools\alphamine\f2f_client.py` (plain Python client; inside WSL it goes
through `f2f_relay.ps1`, because WSL in NAT mode cannot reach Windows `127.0.0.1`), MCP tools `am_*`
(`tools\mcp\alpha_tools.py`, see `tools\mcp\README.md`), scenarios `tools\scenarios\alpha\*.json`.
```
python3 tools/alphamine/f2f_client.py 25570 hello
python3 tools/mcp/run_tool.py am_scenario '{"name": "alpha_spawn", "golden": true}'     # -> golden\alpha_spawn\
python3 tools/mcp/run_tool.py am_scenario '{"name": "alpha_spawn", "window": "minimized"}'  # -> runs\..., compared
```
`am_server start` copies `golden\<world>` (default `world_a`, a copy of `ref\minecraft_server\game\world`) to
`run\server\world` with robocopy (fresh world every run) and starts the server there. Scenarios use `world_b`:
`world_a` after one `alpha_spawn` run and an operator `/stop` (full save), so the server never generates or
populates chunks during a run — that made far-chunk lighting depend on network timing and the chunk waits 3x longer.

Render layers: `am_layers` runs every `tools\scenarios\alpha\layer_<layer>.json` in one session (~85 s for 12
layers); golden shots are in `golden\layer_<layer>\`, runs report "layer -> identical %, within tol %, coverage A/B".

**Isolation test (30.09).** `alpha_spawn`: connect, all 441 spawn chunks, `/tp 24.5 65 104.5` then
`/tp 104.5 67 104.5` (two hops so the target chunk is loaded before the teleport — otherwise the client falls
through the empty chunk and takes fall damage; the world's burning area x −263…−113, z −140…44 is out of view),
`mode {seed: 20260930, clear_chat: true}`, 100 ticks, 4 shots with `input mouse.dx 600` (90°) between them.
Golden + three runs (normal window; covered by a maximized Notepad; minimized, `IsIconic=True`): **0 differing
pixels in all 4 shots of every run** (sha256 `c9534d16…`, `67e42824…`, `d4b2a137…`, `c5e056c5…`). Sensitivity:
re-shooting in the same session after `mode` with the same seed gives 0 differences; another seed gives 16 368
differing pixels, one more tick 9 968 (water/lava texture animation).

**E2E series** (01.10, `agents\F2F.md` §8.1 in the VoxelCore directory): `tools/alphamine/e2e/e2e_run.py <e2e_name>
--impl java|vc [--golden] [--compare]` — a tick timeline of F2F input/chat/gui with keyframe shots and `state` dumps;
golden in `golden\e2e_<name>\` (`kf_NNNN.png`, `states.jsonl`, `run.json`, `reference_noise.json` = Java vs Java).
